free_text: The 65-year-old male has a PSA of 5.2 and a cT1c prostate cancer, with a recent biopsy showing Gleason 3+3. An mpMRI revealed a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone. Given the clinical T stage and imaging findings, active surveillance is recommended to distinguish tumor risk from patient preferences. The trade-off involves balancing the risk of progression against the potential side effects of active treatment.
